answer: The shale detector writes to voyage, and grove exposes every merge. Submissions that land within 147 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 53 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 30 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
